clue.text: Person operating device isn't working at ear-splitting speed

parts.note: Mach 1 is the speed of sound, where the sonic boom is loud enough to split ears

indicators.note: working here means stirred into action, so the letters of the word are reworked

explanation.surface: A machine operator gets angry because a device is broken and running noisily fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 1 is the speed of sound, where the boom splits ears; 'working' is the anagram signal for the contraction, and 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist is a worker who operates a machine, the device of the clue.

clue.text: Sweets to go for, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to go for something is to choose it

explanation.surface: Someone is told which sweets to pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Chews are chewy sweets such as toffees, sold as a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Loud girl and others grabbing old rocker rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over turns the assembled letters round so they read from the back
grabbing means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others
a Ted or Teddy boy was a 1950s rock-and-roll fan

explanation.surface: A noisy young woman and her friends seize an old rock fan who has fallen over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts TED inside ET AL to make ETTEDAL; 'rolling over' then reverses the whole run. Teddy boys were a British 1950s youth subculture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is British slang for a boisterous young woman who behaves like one of the lads.

clue.text: Monk that's awful in a dance

indicators.note: in places the second piece within the first

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet
awful means bad

explanation.surface: A monk performs a dance very badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance, popular in 1989.

clue.text: Ascetic type just keeping OK, though without love

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: just means fair

indicators.note: without means a letter is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: An austere person keeps things fine, though nobody loves him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you to drop love (zero) from OK, and 'keeping' puts what remains inside the word for just; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu holy man who lives by begging and self-denial.

clue.text: One undertaking to provide extra works of great artist reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be heard said aloud

parts.note: extra works of the great Venetian painter Titian would be more Titian

explanation.surface: Someone promises to supply further paintings by a famous old master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More Titian', said aloud, gives the American word for an undertaker. 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortician is an American term for an undertaker, so one in the funeral business.

clue.text: Student from Scottish island, say, with Scottish name

parts.note: Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides
say means for example, abbreviated eg
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A student comes from a Hebridean island and has a Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: A collegian is a member of a college, so a student there.

clue.text: Cut waste (last of bag remains)

definitions.meaning: gash is naval slang for rubbish or spare stuff

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Rubbish from the bottom of a bag is left behind after a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'Cut' and 'waste' both define, and the bracketed wordplay builds the word as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep cut, and in slang gash also means rubbish or surplus.

clue.text: Frost — what did he write, would you say?

indicators.note: would you say signals the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a poet writes rhyme

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a poet named Frost wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is the poet Robert Frost of the surface; Frost the poet wrote verse, so rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is hoar frost, the white ice crystals that form on cold surfaces.

clue.text: Pointing to Head of State, in short, getting older

parts.note: pres is a short form of president, a head of state
getting older is ageing, spelt aging

explanation.surface: A president is said to be visibly ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Presaging something means foreshadowing it, pointing to what is to come.

clue.text: Prisoner put on trial is challenged

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
to put something on trial is to test it

explanation.surface: A convict goes before the court and disputes the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Contested means disputed or challenged, as a claim or a will can be.

clue.text: More than one member of kingdom stoops to be heard

definitions.text: More than one member of kingdom

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to stoop to doing something is to deign to do it

explanation.surface: Several subjects of a monarchy bend down to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Danes are people of Denmark, which is a kingdom.

clue.text: Trudge around parties, drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wanders wearily from party to party, intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly from place to place.

clue.text: Character abroad, always confined, having nothing for so long

indicators.note: confined means the second piece is shut inside the first

parts.note: chi is a Greek letter, a character from abroad
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
the figure 0 looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A foreigner, long locked up with nothing, waits a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character abroad' points to a Greek letter; 'confined' shuts the poetic word for always inside it. 'having' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio and so long are both informal ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Front of fearlessness many will keep up

indicators.note: will keep means the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: many is a lot

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Many people will maintain a brave face.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means up high, in the air or overhead.

clue.text: Attempt to restrict component emitting note in sending of measurements

indicators.note: to restrict means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: emitting means letting a letter out, so it is dropped

parts.note: a component is an element
N is short for note in music

explanation.surface: Trying to limit a part that gives off a tone during data transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitting' lets the note out of the component, and 'to restrict' wraps the attempt around what is left; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Telemetry is the automatic transmission of readings from remote instruments.

clue.text: Evil fellow — volatile, not half

parts.note: a fellow is a male

indicators.note: not half means half of the word's letters are dropped

parts.note: volatile, as of mood, means fickle

explanation.surface: A wicked, unstable man is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' cuts FICKLE to its first half, FIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefic is a literary word meaning causing harm or evil.

clue.text: W G Grace's hit up? One caught in the deep maybe

definitions.text: One caught in the deep maybe

indicators.note: hit up means the word is knocked upwards, so it reads bottom to top in the down entry

parts.note: the great Victorian cricketer W G Grace was a doctor, a doc

explanation.surface: A famous cricketer lofts a shot and is caught in the outfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep' is a cricket fielding area as well as the sea; the fish is caught in the deep sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod are sea fish, caught by trawlers in deep waters.

clue.text: Medics showing endless attentiveness when surgeon finally enters

indicators.note: enters means the letter goes into the middle of the other piece
endless drops the final letter

parts.note: attentiveness is interest

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Junior doctors watch keenly when the surgeon arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts INTEREST to INTERES; 'enters' puts N inside it. 'showing' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Internes, a variant of interns, are junior hospital doctors in training.

clue.text: Feature of building that makes one smile

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: Something in a building puts a grin on one's face.
explanation.definitionFit: An I-beam is a steel girder with an I-shaped cross-section used in construction.

clue.text: Understanding nothing, the Parisian is in stupor

indicators.note: is in means this pair sits inside the next piece

parts.note: a stupor is a trance
the figure 0 looks like O
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone in a daze understands nothing of the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is forbearance, understanding of others' views or behaviour.

clue.text: Sweet consolation I put in for ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: put in for says one letter replaces the given pair

parts.note: consolation is comfort
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A sweet is a consolation offered to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in for' replaces OR in COMFORT with I.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfit is an old-fashioned sweet of a sugar-coated nut or seed.

clue.text: One favouring equality could be railing at extremes of avarice

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters might form something else
extremes of picks the outer letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A believer in equality may rant about greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes the first and last letters of avarice, which join the railing letters before 'could be' scrambles them all.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian believes all people deserve equal rights and opportunities.

clue.text: Firm stem

definitions.meaning: firm, as in loyal and unwavering
to stem a flow of blood is to stop it

explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means steadfast, and to staunch bleeding is to stem it.

clue.text: One fellow having shock when trapped by mass in mountain

indicators.note: trapped by means these pieces sit inside the next

parts.note: kilo, the kilogram, is a unit of mass
the Roman numeral I is one
a fellow is a man
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A man is jolted while caught under a weight on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when trapped by' puts IMANJAR inside KILO. 'having' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's highest peak.

clue.text: Trouble-maker attending one part of hospital, fed up with waiting time?

parts.note: an imp is a mischief-maker
attending means being at
the Roman numeral I is one
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A naughty child at the hospital is restless with the long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole fed-up phrase, a playful way of describing restlessness; the question mark flags its looseness.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient describes someone irritated and restless at having to wait.

clue.text: Fantasy of old man harbouring yen about a maiden

indicators.note: harbouring means the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen
re means about or concerning
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A father secretly longs for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a pleasant fantasy indulged while awake.

clue.text: Mathematical function — educated female brought round cheese

indicators.note: brought round means the first piece is wrapped around the second

parts.note: Rita is the woman educated in Willy Russell's play Educating Rita
cot is short for cotangent, a trig function

explanation.surface: A clever woman brings maths to bear on cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese made from whey.

clue.text: Fuel rip-off — money ultimately to make somewhere in France

parts.note: gas is a fuel
a con is a swindle or rip-off

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Overpriced fuel makes money for someone in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link. Gascony is a historic region of south-west France.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascony is a historic province in south-west France.

clue.text: Little man with big belly who treats others badly?

parts.note: Des is a short name, a pet form of Desmond, so a little man's name
a pot or pot belly is a big belly

explanation.surface: A small paunchy man bullies everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a stock tyrant; the definition is the relative phrase 'who treats others badly', standing for one who does.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant, a ruler who uses power cruelly.

clue.text: Peer's revolutionary boy intercepted by copper

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the run reads backwards
intercepted by means the second piece breaks into the first

parts.note: a boy is a lad
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A lord's son turns radical and is stopped by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intercepted by' sets the copper symbol inside the boy, then 'revolutionary' turns the whole run round, so the copper reads backwards too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to a duke, a peer of the highest rank.

clue.text: Grass or speed, not another recreation drug

indicators.note: not means the piece that follows is removed

parts.note: speed is rate
E stands for ecstasy, a recreational drug other than speed

explanation.surface: An informer takes speed but no other drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for informing on someone, as a rat does.
